claims.text: Oxidation resistance and material integrity in high-temperature MPEAs are governed by their ability to form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 layer.
A critical aluminum concentration enables formation of the protective Al2O3 layer.
A continuous Al2O3 layer slows oxygen diffusion.
Suppressing oxygen diffusion through the oxide scale preserves alloy strength.
At or above the critical aluminum concentration, high-temperature exposure produces a continuous and adherent Al2O3 layer.
The continuous Al2O3 scale limits further oxidation.
The continuous Al2O3 scale limits degradation of mechanical properties during high-temperature oxidation.
MPEAs with lower aluminum concentrations form discontinuous oxide layers or less-protective oxides.
Discontinuous or less-protective oxides cause accelerated oxidation.
Alloys at or above the critical aluminum concentration will have lower mass gains than sub-threshold alloys.
Alloys at or above the critical aluminum concentration will develop a uniform, adherent Al2O3 scale.
Alloys at or above the critical aluminum concentration will retain mechanical properties better than sub-threshold alloys.
Sub-threshold aluminum alloys are expected to form non-protective, discontinuous oxide scales.
Sub-threshold aluminum alloys are expected to exhibit higher oxidation rates and diminished mechanical performance.
The proposed behavior should hold near 1000–1200°C over exposures of at least approximately 100 hours.
The proposed behavior may not apply to short-duration exposures or environments with substantially different chemical aggressiveness.
